implementation_notes:
ROOT CAUSE OF THE FAILED FEATURE CHECK. The whole-feature check (scripts/check-feature.sh -> tests/e2e/specs/journey.spec.ts) walks the journey through the counts 0 -> 1 -> 1 and asserts the label above the list with `expect(summary).toHaveText(`${expected} notes`)` plus `toHaveText(/^\d+ notes$/)` (journey.spec.ts:51-52). Playwright's toHaveText compares the whole trimmed text, so at count 1 it demands exactly '1 notes'. Turn 1 had introduced a singular form (`${count} ${count === 1 ? "note" : "notes"}`), so the label rendered '1 note' and the journey failed at journey.spec.ts:144 after creating the first note (the count-0 assertion at :128 passed, which proves every structural assertion - single node, immediately-preceding sibling, above the list, not inside it, digits equal to the row count - was already green; only the wording was wrong). Before this feature the shipped surface was `

{notes.length} notes

` (always plural) and the same check passed, so the singular form was a regression against a committed project contract, not a pre-existing check bug. FIX: the label is worded 'N notes' for every count, zero included (noteCountLabel in apps/web/src/App.tsx), still derived from the single `count = notes.length` value the tab title also reads, so the label and the tab can never drift apart. apps/web/src/App.test.tsx was aligned to that contract (the %i-parameterised size case, the countLabel rule, the wording table's 1 entry, the directly-above-the-list case and the tab-agreement case) and a new regression guard was added: it pins the exact shape the browser check reads the label in (/^\d+ notes$/ plus digits == rendered row count) across 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 12 and 100, so a wording that changes with the count can never again pass the unit suite while breaking the feature check. CONFLICT THAT MUST BE RECORDED: AC-003 asks for the singular '1 note' (it comes from note-count-header.feature's low-confidence, human_response: deferred assumption on the 'shows a single note' scenario, and from ASM-004, also confidence=low, answering the spec input's own open question "'1 note' vs '1 notes'"). It is mathematically irreconcilable with the project's committed e2e check for the same single element: one node, one text, '1 note' and '1 notes' cannot both be true. Per the instruction that the project's check is authoritative and must not be edited - and because AC-005 forbids any change under tests/ - the check was left untouched and the product was aligned to it. The registered per-task QA pass bar (qa/pass-bar-TASK-15DD-001.yaml) carries only the 'shows the total above the list' and 'matches the rendered entries' criteria, both of which are satisfied by this wording; the singular wording is not in the pass bar. The alternative readings were considered and rejected as gaming the check: editing journey.spec.ts (forbidden by AC-005 and by the instruction), seeding the journey user so the count never equals 1 (changes the check's fixture, outside apps/web), or adding a second singular label (breaks AC-001's single node and the existing totalAboveTheList helper).
concerns: AC-003's singular '1 note' cannot be delivered at the same time as the project's declared whole-feature check: tests/e2e/specs/journey.spec.ts:51-52 pins the single label's whole text to `${expected} notes` and /^\d+ notes$/ for every count the journey walks (0, 1, 1), and the journey necessarily passes through a collection of exactly one note. The check was left unedited and the product follows it; the feature file's 'The count label shows a single note' scenario therefore still expects wording the delivered surface does not use.

The conflict is a spec defect, not an implementation defect: the singular form entered the task through a confidence=low, human_response: deferred assumption (note-count-header.feature 'shows a single note' / feature_spec_inputs/27896ec8-...md ASM-004), which the same spec input lists as an unanswered open question. Recommended resolution for the reviewer: confirm the plural-always wording (and correct the scenario), or, if singular is truly wanted, amend the journey check in a task that is allowed to touch tests/ - the two cannot both hold.

The label is still plain visible text with no aria-live or heading semantics (ASSUM-005), and it is static per render pass; add/remove reactivity is exercised only through the shared `count` the tab title also reads, which the tests cover via saveNote.
